newsitem.title: USA: Allegheny Teledyne CEO to get more therapy.
newsitem.headline: Allegheny Teledyne CEO to get more therapy.

text.p: Richard Simmons, chairman, president and chief executive officer of Allegheny Teledyne Inc, said on Monday that he will undergo follow-up radiotherapy as a precautionary measure, but it will not impair his ability to remain fully engaged as the company's chief executive officer.

"My physicians have advised me that the radiation therapy will not impair my ability to remain fully engaged as Allegheny Teledyne's chief executive officer. Their prognosis indicates that I will 'be able to continue to serve the company for many years,'" Simmons said in a press release.
Simmons noted that in 1996, while he was non-executive chairman of the board of Allegheny Ludlum, he underwent successful cryosurgery to destroy a localized prostate cancer.
He said that a recent biopsy shows no evidence of remaining tumor and the PSA (prostate specific antigen) level remains low.

"Because there has been a slight increase in the PSA levels, although remaining at very low levels, my physicians have recommended that I undergo follow-up radiotherapy as a precautionary measure," he said.

Simmons said that he plans to begin therapy in the next several months following a trip to China to assess the progress of the company's joint venture with Shanghai No. 10 Steel Ltd Co to build and operate a stainless steel strip production facility in China.
